newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state auctions 5 pct of realty firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state auctions 5 pct of realty firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Thursday it was auctioning five percent of its share in partly-private realty firm Heliopolis Housing and Development to one or more strategic investors.
The firm, in which the state currently owns 72.86 percent, said the deadline for bids to buy the 247,238 shares was November 28, 1996. Investors can bid for a minimum one percent.
The new investors will also be entitled to a minimum 9.25 pound ($2.72) dividend for the 1995/96 financial year which ended on June 30, 1996.
The firm said it had raised net after tax profits for 1995/96 to 61.3 million pounds from 34.1 million a year earlier.
It forecast profits of 67.4 million for the current financial year 1996/97.
Net sales for 1995/96 also rose to 238.4 million from 57.7 million a year earlier.
Private investors already hold 17.14 percent of the real estate firm and its workers own another 10 percent.
Last month, the state said it would sell 2.2 million shares in Heliopolis Housing as part of its privatisation programme.

The announcement buoyed the firm's share prices but rumours that the state was cutting back the stake it was offering dampened the uptrend. On Thursday, the stock was trading in a range of 172 and 175 pounds.
